instructions: Trim the green beans and cut them into 2 inch pieces. Dice the onion, chop the tomatoes, and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large wide pot over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook, stirring now and then, for 5 minutes, until it's soft and starting to turn golden.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens a shade.
Add the garlic, allspice and cinnamon. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell them.
Add the green beans and stir for 1 minute, until every bean is coated in the oil.

Add the tomatoes, 1/2 cup water, the remaining 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Stir, then cover and turn the heat to medium-low. Cook for 18 minutes, stirring every 6 minutes, until the beans are soft all the way through.

Meanwhile, rinse the rice in a fine strainer until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt, and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes.
Take the lid off the beans, turn the heat to medium-high, and cook for 3 minutes, until most of the liquid has cooked off and the sauce clings to the beans.
Take the rice off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes. Then fluff it with a fork.
Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley and stir it into the beans off the heat. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the beans over the rice, warm or at room temperature.
method_notes: Both sources braise the green beans in olive oil with onion, garlic and tomato, and cover the pot so the beans soften in their own juices. They differ on oil (3 tbsp in the lead, 1/3 cup in the other), on tomato paste, and on spice: the lead uses only paprika, the other uses baharat. This version keeps the 3 tbsp of oil, adds tomato paste for depth, and uses allspice and cinnamon, the main notes in Lebanese seven spice, so there is no blended spice to check for gluten. It is served over plain basmati rice, not pita or vermicelli rice, so it stays gluten-free and vegan.
